messages:
maria g: Hey — hitting a weird combo of issues with redwoodctl on WSL2 Ubuntu. Install went fine but `redwoodctl local serve` immediately errors with a profile merge failure and then the auth flow loops when I try `redwoodctl login`.

alex r: ugh. can you paste the error you see?

maria g: sure — here's the first part:```
error: failed to merge profiles: invalid character '\u0000' in profiles.json at offset 1024
```then when I try `redwoodctl login` it opens the browser, I paste code, it returns success but `redwoodctl whoami` still says unauthenticated.

kevin t: do you have any symlinked config dirs or mounted drives? WSL path translation sometimes writes a corrupted file if windows process touches it.

maria g: nope, clean WSL home. I did see this in the logs:```
2026-03-18T14:22:11Z ERROR app: profile write failed: write /home/mg/.config/redwood/profiles.json: short write
```

alex r: ah 'short write' usually means the file was truncated mid-write. Two quick workarounds: 1) move the current profiles file aside and re-login: `mv ~/.config/redwood/profiles.json ~/.config/redwood/profiles.json.bak && redwoodctl login` 2) if you rely on multiple profiles, re-create with `redwoodctl profile import --file <json>` after fixing the truncated file.

maria g: moving aside fixed the auth loop, thanks. But `local serve` still fails with `k8s: context "redwood-local" not found` even though I thought local mode should auto-create a kind-of ephemeral kube context?

kevin t: local serve requires a local kube config to talk to the dev runtime (we don't run an in-process emulator anymore). You can run `redwoodctl local init` which will prompt to install a lightweight k3s cluster (or you can point `KUBECONFIG` at a KinD/k3s cluster). We should make that clearer in the installer UX.

maria g: mhm, `redwoodctl local init` hangs for me at "waiting for cluster" on WSL — logs show systemd not available. Is there a recommended WSL instrux?

alex r: for WSL we recommend using Docker Desktop + k3d instead of systemd-backed k3s. Try: `curl -fsSL https://get.redwood.ai/local-init.sh | bash` then choose k3d. Or manually: `k3d cluster create redwood-local --agents 1` and export `KUBECONFIG=$(k3d kubeconfig write redwood-local)`. Then `redwoodctl local serve` should find the context.

maria g: that worked with k3d. two notes that might be bugs: 1) installer script didn't stop when profiles.json was truncated — it just overwrote and produced a zero-byte file once I retried. 2) the login success message says "open browser and enter code" but sometimes the CLI still says not authenticated until you run `redwoodctl refresh-token` — maybe we need better polling/refresh handling.

kevin t: filing a ticket. can you drop the minimal repro steps here? i'll create a devex issue and add you as owner.

maria g: repro steps:
1) Fresh WSL2 Ubuntu user
2) Install via the apt script from our docs
3) Run `redwoodctl login` -> complete browser flow
4) Observe `redwoodctl whoami` returns unauthenticated
5) `mv ~/.config/redwood/profiles.json ~/.config/redwood/profiles.json.bak && redwoodctl login` then `redwoodctl local init` -> hangs on systemd, instead use k3d workaround above.

devex-bot: Thanks — created DE-4217: "redwoodctl installer/profile truncation + auth refresh flakiness on WSL" and assigned to @kevin t. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/DE-4217 :thumbsup:

alex r: thanks — also adding a CLI patch to validate profiles.json on startup and fallback to a safe default if it's corrupted.

maria g: appreciated. posting this in case anyone else hits the same thing. :coffee:
